extracted.intended_audience: marketing and PR professionals, SEO specialists, and businesses issuing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and distributing press releases that comply with Google (2025) search and News policies, avoid SEO penalties, and maximize brand/earned-media impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose: Inform, not manipulate
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should be crafted with the primary goal of informing, not manipulating search rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with journalistic value and real informational worth; avoid promotional fluff or writing designed primarily to influence PageRank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat press releases as a backlink SEO tactic
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases no longer boost SEO through backlinks — Google treats them as promotional content rather than editorial links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid distributing press releases solely to acquire backlinks; focus on brand exposure, referral traffic, and earned media instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid keyword-rich anchor text links
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases stuffed with keyword-rich anchor text links for SEO manipulation are penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use branded or natural anchor text; do not use exact-match keyword anchors; apply nofollow or sponsored attributes when linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mass-syndicated duplicate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass-syndicated, duplicate press releases across multiple low-quality press release sites are considered spammy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute selectively to authoritative outlets, vary headlines/summaries across outlets, and prioritize earned media to prevent duplicate-content penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit dofollow links; prefer nofollow/sponsored
rubrics_metrics.description: Overuse of dofollow links in press releases is seen as an attempt to manipulate PageRank and can lead to penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 0–2 links per release, mark them nofollow or sponsored, and avoid linking to the same page multiple times within the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid low-quality AI-generated content without human review
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated, low-quality content with little journalistic or informational value can be penalized by Google.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI for drafting only; require human editing, fact-checking, and editorial oversight before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure proper attributions and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should include proper attributions and citations to ensure credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite data sources, attribute quotes, and provide verifiable details to strengthen E-E-A-T and journalistic trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-E-A-T compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Google prioritizes Expertise, Experience, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness (E-E-A-T) when giving visibility to press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include author/organization credentials, expert quotes, original data, and verifiable facts to demonstrate E-E-A-T.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, original, newsworthy content
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases that provide unique insights and original newsworthy content rank better than generic promotional pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid promotional fluff; include novel facts, data, or clear news hooks that warrant editorial attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline standards: short, clear, newsworthy (under 70 characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a strong, newsworthy headline that is clear, compelling, and keyword-optimized without being clickbait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headlines under 70 characters, include a relevant keyword naturally, use action words, and avoid keyword stuffing or unnatural formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph answers journalistic questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening paragraph should answer Who, What, When, Where, Why, and How.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide immediate value and set a neutral, journalistic tone rather than sounding overly promotional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise and scannable format (400–800 words; short paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should be between 400–800 words and formatted for skimmability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short paragraphs (2–3 sentences), subheadings, bullet points, and scannable structure to improve readability and News compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking strategy: 1–2 relevant links with attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only 1–2 relevant links (such as homepage or a landing page) and apply nofollow or sponsored attributes to avoid penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not link multiple times to the same page; prefer branded or natural anchor text and limit the total number of links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a clear CTA and media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Every press release should end with a clear call to action and press contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide email, website, location, and other PR contact info; journalists prefer clear media contact details for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human oversight for AI-assisted writing
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can assist writing, but human review and editing are mandatory to meet Google’s quality standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-check, personalize, add expert commentary, and ensure editorial quality before publishing AI-assisted content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add unique insights and expert quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Including original data, expert commentary, or company insights helps a press release stand out and satisfy E-E-A-T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes from named experts and proprietary data points to create editorial value and increase chances of pickup by journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetitive phrasing and keyword overuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetitive, formulaic language and keyword stuffing (common in AI drafts) reduce quality and risk penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write natural language flows, vary phrasing, and avoid over-optimization of keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution to high-authority platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of mass distribution, submit press releases to high-traffic media sites, industry publications, and niche outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize PR Newswire, Business Wire, Google News-approved sites, and direct pitches to reputable outlets rather than low-quality PR directories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch journalists and pursue earned media (HARO, influencers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct journalist outreach and earned media are more effective than mass PR wire distribution for credibility and SEO impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use HARO, industry journalist networks, and influencer collaborations to get editorial coverage that can lead to natural backlinks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Google News & Featured Snippet optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Format press releases for Google News and Featured Snippets to improve visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise news-style headlines (<70 chars), include a dateline, structure with short paragraphs and subheadings, and optimize meta descriptions (under 160 characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use structured data (Schema Markup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add NewsArticle structured data and other relevant schema to help Google recognize press releases as news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement NewsArticle schema; consider Organization schema for brand attribution and FAQ schema to improve SERP visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage multimedia effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Including images, videos, or infographics increases engagement and the likelihood of Google News visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one high-resolution image with descriptive alt text, use YouTube-hosted videos for discoverability, and consider interactive elements (GIFs, motion graphics) to boost engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on press releases for link building
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing press releases solely to obtain backlinks violates Google’s Link Scheme Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on strategies that earn editorial coverage and organic backlinks rather than relying on PR wires to pass PageRank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize for future search formats (voice & AI summaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare press releases for conversational/voice search and AI summarization (SGE, Discover).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise phrases that answer likely questions, structure content for AI summarizers, and consider conversational query phrasing to improve voice search relevance.
